title: SLO attack mitigation and rapid stabilization guide
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This guide documents the playbook we use when an SLO deviation or large-scale latency/cost regression ("SLO attack") is detected across multiple services or customers. The objective is to stabilize user-visible behavior within the first 30 minutes, protect higher-priority customers, and preserve evidence for post-incident analysis. This doc is intended for on-call engineers, SREs, and incident commanders.

When to use this playbook

Use this playbook when any of the following trigger conditions are met: 
- Platform-level latency P50/P95/P99 exceeds configured SLO thresholds for > 3 minutes across 2+ regions.
- Error rate spike (5xx or model-serving failures) > 2x baseline sustained for > 5 minutes.
- Sudden consumption or cost anomaly indicating runaway token generation or abusive traffic.
- Multiple customer-facing routes degrade simultaneously without isolated root cause.

Quick summary (first 30 minutes)

1) Acknowledge and open an incident in the incident tracker and bridge. Required fields: impact (customers affected), regions, earliest observed time, initial SLO metrics.
2) Put a short status update to the status page (see template below) marked "investigating".
3) Identify and attach the on-call runbook owners: serving-runtime, edge-proxy, routing, and billing.
4) Apply immediate mitigations (rate-limit, throttle, fallback models) following the Mitigation Matrix.
5) Preserve logs and snapshots: export relevant Prometheus ranges, JVM/Docker logs, and KV cache stats.

Ownership and roles

- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates responders, decides customer-facing messaging, and owns postmortem.
- Primary Responder(s): owns triage of a specific subsystem (serving-runtime, load-balancer, routing).
- Safety Operator: applies throttles, API key blocks, or routing fallbacks.
- Metrics/Telemetry Lead: validates and publishes SLO metrics and confirms whether mitigation improves signals.
- Customer Liaison (CS/Support): drafts and posts customer comms for impacted signups.

Escalation ladder

| Role | When to escalate | Contact method |
|---|---:|---|
| Primary Responder -> IC | No progress after 15 minutes or unclear root cause | Pager, then Slack @incident-ops |
| IC -> Engineering Lead | 30 minutes without stabilization or potential broad outage | Phone + Exec Slack |
| IC -> Legal/Security | Suspicion of abuse, data exposure, or regulatory impact | Pager to Legal on-call |

Measurement and tooling checklist

- Dashboards: platform-slo-overview, model-serving-latency, api-traffic-origins, kv-cache-misses.
- Prometheus queries to run quickly:
  - Platform P95 (last 5m): sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{le=\"0.5\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_count[5m]))  // adjust as needed
  - Error rate (5xx) per route: increase(query: rate(http_requests_total{status=~\"5..\"}[5m]))
- Logs: consolidate logs with "incident_id" tag. Use the following command to tail recent errors from serving runtime: 
  - kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=serving-runtime --since=15m --tail=200 | jq '.message' | grep -i error
- Storage/state: snapshot Redis/KV cache sizes and eviction stats: redis-cli INFO stats | egrep 'evicted_keys|used_memory'

Mitigation matrix (ordered: least invasive -> more intrusive)

1) Rate-limit noisy API keys and anonymous traffic
  - Action: apply short TTL block via API gateway with 1-minute window.
  - Owner: Safety Operator.
2) Enable model fallback to smaller quantized variant for non-critical routes
  - Action: update routing policy to route to small-quantized-v2 for routes with latency > 1s
  - Owner: Routing team.
3) Apply progressive global throttling (10% -> 50%) for new sessions
  - Action: set throttle policy in traffic router. Monitor errors closely.
  - Owner: Serving-runtime oncall.
4) Disable non-essential background batches (cache warmers, telemetry ingestion)
  - Action: flip feature flag \"background-workers.enabled\" = false
  - Owner: Platform infra.
5) Emergency capacity burst (if Dedicated customers permit)
  - Action: trigger reserved burst pool; notify capacity team.
  - Owner: SRE lead.

Detailed triage workflow (structured)

Step 0 — Incident open and classify (0–5 minutes):
- IC records scope and initial metrics, assigns owners.
- Post initial status page message.

Step 1 — Containment (5–15 minutes):
- Apply rate-limits to noisy sources. Use monitoring to verify immediate effect.
- Route traffic away from failing region if the blast radius is regional: update traffic-router to prefer other regions.

Step 2 — Root-cause narrowing (15–45 minutes):
- Correlate deploys: check CI/CD deploy events in the last 30 minutes (Jenkins/GitHub Actions).
- Validate model artifacts: checksum and size mismatch between model variants.
- Check kernel/scheduling logs for OOMs, GPU driver resets: dmesg, nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv
- Confirm whether a KV cache spike or miss storm is present (cache-miss-rate > 5x baseline).

Step 3 — Stabilize & validate (45–90 minutes):
- If mitigations improved SLOs, start phased rollback of high-impact mitigations (e.g., reduce throttling to 10%).
- Run synthetic checks and customer smoke tests (see Smoke Test Script section).

Post-incident actions (within 72 hours)

- Evidence collection: collect dashboards, logs, the final mitigation list, and timestamps of each action.
- Postmortem: IC authors a RCA-style postmortem using the postmortem template (link below) within 48 hours; final review at 72 hours.
- Action items: translate mitigations and fixes into tracked JIRA issues with owners and due dates.
- SLO adjustment review: if the attack revealed unrealistic SLOs for a route, propose SLO change through the SLO governance board.

Smoke Test Script (quick validation)

1) Local synthetic request for a critical route:
  curl -s -D - -o /dev/null 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?route=chat' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY'
  Expected: 200 within 800ms for P50; check response headers for x-redwood-model and x-request-id.
2) Cold-KV test:
  - Run a request that uses prefix-cache; then inspect cache hit ratio: 
    curl -s 'https://internal-metrics/api/cache/hits?prefix=abc'
  Expected: hit_ratio > 0.6 after warmup
3) Model fallback verification:
  - Trigger a forced fallback in staging: /admin/fallback?route=chat&variant=small-quantized-v2
  - Validate latency and output quality against golden examples.

Status page and customer comms templates

- Status page short update (investigating):
  "title: Investigating increased API latency in us-west-2
   impact: Customers in us-west-2 may see elevated request latency or transient errors.
   what_we_are_doing: Investigating root cause, applying rate-limits and fallbacks as needed.
   next_update: in 15 minutes"

- Status page follow-up (stabilizing):
  "title: Service stabilizing — mitigation applied
   impact: Elevated latency reduced after routing fallbacks and throttles. Some customers may still experience intermittent errors.
   what_we_did: Applied API key rate-limits and routed non-critical traffic to quantized models.
   next_update: in 60 minutes or sooner"

- Customer email template (high-impact, actionable):
  "Subject: Incident update — platform latency impacting API requests

  Hi <Customer Name>,

  We are investigating an issue that began at <time>. You may have experienced higher-than-normal latency or transient errors for requests to <routes>. Our engineers have applied mitigations to reduce impact and are actively monitoring. We will follow up with a detailed post-incident report and action items.

  Immediate recommendations for you: use the \"retry with backoff\" pattern, pause background batch jobs if any, and reach out to <Customer Success rep> if you see persistent issues.

  Sincerely,
  Redwood Operations"

Game day & rehearsal guidance (quarterly)

Purpose: exercise SLO-attack scenarios that cross multiple subsystems (routing, serving runtime, KV cache). Run frequency: quarterly; duration: 2–4 hours.

Game day outline:
- Pre-brief (15 minutes): objectives, success criteria, and safe-failures.
- Injects (each 10–30 minutes): noisy-API-key flood, model artifact corruption (checksum mismatch), KV cache miss storm, and region network partition.
- Observation: Metrics lead must produce a stabilization dashboard within 20 minutes.
- After-action (60 minutes): short retro; capture 3 concrete action items.

Success criteria for the drill

- Incident acknowledged within 5 minutes.
- Initial mitigation applied within 15 minutes.
- Recover to within 10% of normal P95 latency within 60 minutes unless the scenario is intentionally unrecoverable.

Attachments and links

- Postmortem template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-template-standard
- CI/CD deploy feed: https://ci.redwood.internal/deploys
- Key dashboards: dashboard://platform-slo-overview, dashboard://model-serving-latency
- Runbook for API gateway rate-limits: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/api-gateway-rate-limits

Examples of past mitigations (learning log)

- 2026-05-18: Large KV eviction storm mitigated by disabling cache-warmers; lead to rule that producers must not exceed 200QPS to cache.
- 2026-10-02: Traffic spike from new client SDK version; created auto-detection rule for client version churn.

Revision history

- 2026-11-04: Initial draft authored by Maya Chen.
- 2026-12-15: Added PromQL quick queries and new mitigation step for background workers (Priya Rao).
- 2027-01-12: Formalized game day success criteria and templates (Diego Alvarez).

If you have feedback or want to run a custom game day for your team, contact the SRE lead or add a comment on this page.
